facts.text: Auto-GCAS (Automatic Ground Collision Avoidance System) takes control of F-16 and F-35 fighter aircraft and pulls the aircraft up when a collision with the ground is imminent.
facts.quote: Auto-GCAS is the system on F-16 and F-35 fighter aircraft that takes control and pulls the aircraft up when it is about to fly into the ground

facts.text: Auto-GCAS grew out of research by NASA, the US Air Force Research Laboratory and Lockheed Martin dating to the early 1980s.
facts.quote: grew out of research by NASA, the US Air Force Research Laboratory and Lockheed Martin dating to the early 1980s.

facts.text: Auto-GCAS retrofits on F-16 Block 40 and 50 aircraft began in September 2014.
facts.quote: Retrofits on F-16 Block 40 and 50 aircraft began in September 2014

facts.text: Auto-GCAS integration on F-35 aircraft followed in 2019; the manufacturer says reuse of the F-16 work brought integration seven years earlier than previously planned.
facts.quote: F-35 integration followed in 2019, which the manufacturer says came "seven years earlier than previously planned" thanks to reuse of the F-16 work

facts.text: By the time of F-35 integration in 2019, Auto-GCAS was credited with saving eight F-16 pilots' lives.
facts.quote: with eight F-16 pilots' lives credited as saved by then

facts.text: A 2007 NASA release reported 98 percent effectiveness for Auto-GCAS.
facts.quote: A 2007 NASA release reported 98 percent effectiveness [Chapter 2].

facts.text: Auto-GCAS had a design requirement to be nuisance free; the test lead prioritized ensuring no harm and no nuisance before providing protection.
facts.quote: "It's only if we can make sure we're not going to do any harm, and not be a nuisance, only then will we worry about providing protection"

facts.text: Flight testing remained part of the Auto-GCAS program throughout.
facts.quote: Flight testing remained part of the program throughout.

facts.text: Auto-GCAS is an automatic flight-control recovery and is a precedent for automatic intervention rather than object-triggered braking.
facts.quote: Auto-GCAS is an automatic flight-control recovery, so it is an analog for intervention rather than for object-triggered braking

facts.text: Acceptance of Auto-GCAS came from the US Air Force, not a civil regulator.
facts.quote: its acceptance came from the US Air Force, not a civil regulator [Chapter 2].

facts.text: Auto-GCAS compressed validation time through reuse only after about three decades of foundational work, supporting the booklet's conclusion that reuse is fast and first construction is slow.
facts.quote: Auto-GCAS is a real case of validation time compressed by reuse, but only after about three decades of foundational work, which supports the booklet's conclusion that reuse is fast and first construction is slow

facts.text: The booklet recommends Auto-GCAS's nuisance-first philosophy for a machine brake: prove that the brake does no harm and does not annoy before proving that it protects.
facts.quote: Its nuisance-first philosophy is the one the booklet recommends for a machine brake: prove it does no harm and does not annoy, then prove it protects [Chapters 2, 4].
